items.title: CVD benefits of semaglutide not fully explained by weight loss
items.summary: The cardiovascular benefits of the GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide cannot be fully explained by weight loss or improvements in other known risk factors, according to a new analysis of a major clinical trial.

items.summary: British Journal of Midwifery, Volume 34, Issue 10, Page 548-559, October 2026.…

items.title: Evidence is ‘reassuring’ for women who become pregnant while taking GLP-1 drugs
items.summary: Exposure to GLP-1 weight-loss and diabetes drugs around conception does not appear to be linked to a detectable increase in adverse outcomes for mothers or babies, a large review of the evidence has concluded.

items.title: GLP-1s and SGLT-2s may help slow kidney damage in diabetes, study shows
items.summary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists and sodium glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor drugs slow decline in kidney function in people with type 2 diabetes, but the benefits are only seen if they also have albuminuria, a large US ‘real-world’ study has reported.

items.title: Semaglutide linked to 40% reduction in asthma attacks
items.summary: Weight loss and diabetes treatment semaglutide is associated with a nearly 40% reduction in asthma attacks among people with the condition, according to new analysis.

items.title: UK watchdog rebukes Eli Lilly over GLP-1 press release sent to BBC
items.summary: A UK watchdog found an Eli Lilly GLP-1 press release sent to the BBC used 'promotional and emotive' language and brought discredit on the pharmaceutical industry, per Fierce Pharma.

items.title: Weight-loss injections cut obesity rates in children, study finds
items.summary: Two-in-five children living with obesity achieved a body mass index (BMI) below the obesity threshold when taking weight-loss injections, a new study has found.

items.title: Guidelines on weight-loss drugs before and after pregnancy show stark gaps in evidence
items.summary: New guidelines developed to support the safe use of GLP-1 medicines before, during and after pregnancy are limited by gaps in the evidence, the researchers who developed them have said.

items.title: BMA semaglutide guidance is welcome but dated
items.summary: Copperfield is less than pleased with the BMA’s outdated reminder that GPs must not prescribe semaglutide for CVD risk without ‘written confirmation’ of funding from ICBs Two cheers for the BMA. Remember TA1152?

items.title: GPs must not prescribe semaglutide for CVD risk without ‘written confirmation’ of funding
items.summary: GP practices and LMCs should ask for ‘written confirmation’ of commissioning from ICBs before prescribing semaglutide for cardiovascular risk reduction, the BMA has advised.
